paper.title: A Mechanistic Theory Unifying Value and Schema in the Prefrontal Cortex
paper.abstract: Animals exhibit behavioural flexibility by making reward-optimal decisions in unfamiliar situations. Computing value from minimal reward feedback requires leveraging known structure in the world. The Prefrontal Cortex (PFC) plays a pivotal role in both value computation and learning world structure, however mechanistic explanations for each---within the frameworks of Reinforcement Learning and Cognitive Maps---are largely distinct. We develop a mechanistic model of PFC that unifies value and structure through behavioural flexibility. In this model, value acts as a control signal that gates structured working memory representations of the current context in order to ultimately control behaviour. This is a significant departure from the conventional perspective of value, in which it is used for action readout. Critically, this model generalises to novel contexts without the need for additional synaptic plasticity. We demonstrate that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) meta-trained with either reinforcement learning or supervised learning recapitulate this exact model on various value-based tasks. These results not only provide a parsimonious explanation of both the value and schema frameworks of PFC function, but also propose a new mechanistic interpretation of the role of PFC in flexible decision making.

paper.title: Cellular-resolution Three-photon Ultra-Deep Imaging (TrUDI) of neuronalpopulation activity at 2 mm depth in the mammalian brain
paper.abstract: Extending the depth reach of multi-photon microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an exponentially hard problem. Three-photon (3p) microscopy has enabled imaging of neuroactivity at depths up to ~1.2 mm in the mouse brain. However, the fundamental depth limit of 3p imaging, as set by the depth at which the out-of-focus background fluorescence exceeds the in-focus fluorescence signal, is well beyond 2 mm. Reaching this fundamental depth limit in 3p imaging has been hampered by insufficient in-focus fluorescence signal arising from suboptimal optical design and acquisition conditions. Here, we demonstrate a Three-photon Ultra-Deep Imaging (TrUDI) system that approaches this fundamental depth limit via systematic and principled optimization of the in-focus fluorescence signal. TrUDI optimally matches the parameters of the excitation laser, the optical system, and the acquisition to linear and non-linear limits for safe laser exposure. At the same time, TrUDI remains compatible with the spatial and temporal requirements for single-cell resolution calcium imaging, and its parameters are tuned to the photo-physics of 3p excitation and the scattering properties of the mouse brain tissue. Our approach results in a ~250-fold increase in detected fluorescence photons at the same laser power as in previous approaches. We use TrUDI to demonstrate in vivo cellular-resolution recordings of neuronal population activity within fields of view of ~230 x 230 um2 at 8.6 Hz at tissue depths of up to ~2 mm in mouse cortex and hippocampus.

paper.title: NeuroPilot: Longitudinal intravital neural imaging across scales and modalities through an agentic platform
paper.abstract: Longitudinal intravital imaging is essential for understanding how neural populations evolve across behavioral states, yet converting large-scale recordings into biological insight remains a fundamental challenge because neural signals are degraded by noise, non-rigid motion, and heterogeneous recording conditions. Here we introduce NeuroPilot, an agentic framework that transforms neural imaging analysis into a closed-loop, context-aware process, integrating a multimodal large language model with callable computational imaging modules to adaptively coordinate workflows from raw recordings to population-level readouts. Across heterogeneous imaging and experimental regimes, NeuroPilot restores motion-degraded recordings and supports consistent neural signal recovery, detection, and tracking in challenging deep-brain, freely moving, and longitudinal settings. These enable neuronal population tracking across spinal stimulation paradigms, deep-brain imaging, and continuous 24-hour mPFC recordings aligned with spontaneous sleep-wake behavior. By converting heterogeneous intravital recordings into stable population activity maps, NeuroPilot supports behavioral decoding and reveals structured neural dynamics across behavioral states and transitions. NeuroPilot establishes a scalable agentic paradigm for neural imaging analysis, expanding experimental access to the measurement, visualization, and interpretation of neural population activity.
